An operator following .env.example (which ships all vars with empty defaults) can reach a partially-enabled state: the webhook accepts credential writes while token refresh silently falls back to the local refreshFunction, causing credential data to diverge between the two systems at first token expiry. However, the local refresh path itself still functions correctly (it calls the original provider refresh), so this is not strictly incorrect behavior of the code — it is a real, specific configuration-coupling/operational risk a maintainer would want to know when shipping this feature, not a verifiable defect.

judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gates the webhook write path on CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY but not on CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, while the refresh path in refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse additionally requires the endpoint. An operator who sets the two webhook vars but leaves the endpoint empty (the .env.example ships all four with empty defaults) gets a deployment that accepts credential writes but refreshes locally against placeholder or stale tokens — a partially-enabled state that only fails at first token expiry, far from the config that caused it.

adjudication.rationale: Diff-grounded mismatch: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined only by `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), and the webhook write handler is gated solely on that (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts). But the “sync refresh” behavior is additionally gated on `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` in both `refreshOAuthTokens` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/*). This creates a partially-enabled configuration state (webhook accepts/updates credentials while refresh logic won’t use the external endpoint). Whether it becomes a runtime failure depends on what keys are synced (webhook doesn’t validate key shape), so it’s more of an operational/edge-case footgun than a strictly provable defect from the diff alone.
